notes:
1. Social Justice — Meaning

  • Social justice means creating conditions in which individuals and groups have fair access to rights, opportunities, resources, institutions and dignity.
  • It seeks to reduce unjust disadvantage arising from caste, gender, disability, economic status, social exclusion and geographic isolation.
📌 Must-Memorise

Social Justice → Rights + Representation + Redistribution + Recognition

2. Social Justice vs Poverty Relief

  • Poverty relief primarily addresses economic deprivation.
  • Social justice is broader and asks who receives education, representation, productive resources, institutional access and freedom from discrimination.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Social Justice ≠ Poverty Relief Alone

3. Core Objective of Social Justice

The broad objective is:

Removal of Discrimination

  • Equal Opportunity
  • Corrective Support
  • Social Dignity

4. Formal Equality

  • Formal equality means the same rule applies to everyone.
  • It guarantees equal legal treatment but may not remove disadvantages inherited from unequal social conditions.

5. Substantive Equality

  • Substantive equality recognises that historically disadvantaged groups may require additional support to obtain meaningful opportunities.
  • Examples include reservation, scholarships, disability accommodation and social protection.
📌 Must-Memorise

Unequal Starting Conditions → May Require Differential Support

6. Formal vs Substantive Equality

  • Formal equality → Same rules.
  • Substantive equality → Fair opportunity in practice.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Corrective Measures Do Not Necessarily Contradict Equality

7. Preamble — Justice

The Preamble promises:

  • Social justice.
  • Economic justice.
  • Political justice.
📌 Must-Memorise

Preamble → Justice: Social + Economic + Political

8. Social Justice — Constitutional Meaning

Social justice seeks:

  • Equality.
  • Dignity.
  • Representation.
  • Removal of discrimination.
  • Abolition of untouchability.

9. Economic Justice

Economic justice concerns:

  • Livelihood.
  • Fair wages.
  • Social security.
  • Distribution of resources.
  • Prevention of extreme economic disadvantage.

10. Political Justice

Political justice includes:

  • Universal adult franchise.
  • Political representation.
  • Access to democratic institutions.
  • Meaningful participation.
📌 Must-Memorise

Social + Economic + Political Justice → Democratic Citizenship

11. Article 14

  • Article 14 guarantees:
  • Equality before law.
  • Equal protection of laws.
📌 Must-Memorise

Article 14 → Constitutional Equality

12. Article 15

  • Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds including:
  • Religion.
  • Race.
  • Caste.
  • Sex.
  • Place of birth.
  • It also permits constitutionally authorised affirmative-action measures.

13. Article 16

  • Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity in public employment.
  • It also provides the constitutional framework for reservation in specified circumstances.
📌 Must-Memorise

Article 16 → Public Employment + Representation

14. Article 17

  • Article 17 abolishes untouchability and prohibits its practice in any form.
📌 Must-Memorise

Article 17 → Abolition of Untouchability

15. Article 21

  • Article 21 protects life and personal liberty.
  • The constitutional idea of life with dignity has important social-justice implications.

16. Article 21A

  • Article 21A provides free and compulsory education for children aged 6–14 years.
📌 Must-Memorise

Article 21A → Education → 6–14 Years

17. Articles 23 and 24

  • Article 23 prohibits trafficking, begar and similar forms of forced labour.
  • Article 24 prohibits employment of children below fourteen years in factories, mines and other hazardous employment under the constitutional framework.
📌 Must-Memorise

Article 23 → Exploitation/Forced Labour

Article 24 → Child Labour Protection

18. Fundamental Rights and Social Justice

Fundamental Rights protect individuals from:

  • Discrimination.
  • Untouchability.
  • Exploitation.
  • Denial of equal opportunity.
📌 Must-Memorise

Social Justice Requires Protection from Discrimination + Exploitation

19. Article 38

  • Article 38 directs the State to promote a social order in which justice informs all institutions.
  • It also seeks minimisation of inequalities in:
  • Income.
  • Status.
  • Facilities.
  • Opportunities.
📌 Must-Memorise

Article 38 → Social Order + Reduction of Inequalities

20. Article 39

Article 39 includes principles relating to:

  • Adequate livelihood.
  • Distribution of material resources for the common good.
  • Prevention of concentration of wealth.
  • Equal pay for equal work.
  • Protection of workers and children.

21. Article 41

  • Article 41 concerns State responsibility, within its economic capacity, for:
  • Work.
  • Education.
  • Public assistance in unemployment.
  • Old age.
  • Sickness.
  • Disablement.

22. Article 42

  • Article 42 provides for:
  • Just and humane conditions of work.
  • Maternity relief.
📌 Must-Memorise

Article 42 → Humane Work Conditions + Maternity Relief

23. Article 46

  • Article 46 directs the State to promote the educational and economic interests of weaker sections, particularly:
  • Scheduled Castes.
  • Scheduled Tribes.
  • It also seeks protection from social injustice and exploitation.
📌 Must-Memorise

Article 46 → SC/ST Educational + Economic Advancement

24. Article 47

  • Article 47 places responsibility on the State to improve:
  • Nutrition.
  • Standard of living.
  • Public health.

25. Directive Principles and Social Justice

The Directive Principles connect:

Social Justice

→ Welfare-State Responsibility

→ Public Action

26. Caste Inequality

Historically, caste affected access to:

  • Education.
  • Occupation.
  • Land.
  • Public institutions.
  • Housing.
  • Social status.

27. Untouchability and Social Exclusion

  • Untouchability represented an extreme form of caste exclusion.
  • Article 17 abolished it constitutionally.
  • Legal prohibition, however, does not automatically eliminate social prejudice.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Legal Equality ≠ Automatic Social Equality

28. Caste-Based Social Justice

Effective caste justice requires:

  • Anti-discrimination law.
  • Representation.
  • Educational access.
  • Economic advancement.
  • Social dignity.
  • Changes in public attitudes.

29. Affirmative Action

  • Affirmative action means deliberate measures to improve opportunities for historically disadvantaged or underrepresented groups.
  • Reservation is one important form, but not the only one.

30. Social Justice Beyond Reservation

Other instruments include:

  • Scholarships.
  • Hostels.
  • Educational assistance.
  • Livelihood support.
  • Special institutions.
  • Political representation.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Reservation Alone ≠ Complete Social Justice

31. Representation

Representation matters because public institutions should not remain socially inaccessible.

It can improve:

  • Participation.
  • Administrative legitimacy.
  • Social mobility.
  • Institutional inclusion.
📌 Must-Memorise

Representation → Inclusion → Opportunity

32. Tamil Nadu — 69% Reservation Context

  • Tamil Nadu's reservation framework is an important institutional expression of its social-justice tradition.
  • The detailed constitutional structure and percentages were covered in Chapter 31.
📌 Must-Memorise

Tamil Nadu Social Justice → Representation + Educational Access + Welfare

33. Education as Social Justice

Education weakens the influence of inherited disadvantage because children do not choose:

  • Birth.
  • Caste.
  • Family income.
  • Geographic location.

34. Educational Justice

Educational justice requires:

  • Access.
  • Affordability.
  • Retention.
  • Quality.
  • Higher-education opportunity.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

School Admission Alone ≠ Educational Justice

35. First-Generation Learners

For first-generation learners:

Education

→ Skills

→ Employment

→ Income

→ Intergenerational Mobility

📌 Must-Memorise

Education → Major Route from Inherited Disadvantage to Mobility

36. Economic Justice

Economic justice seeks to prevent extreme disadvantage from blocking basic opportunities.

Important areas include:

  • Employment.
  • Fair wages.
  • Social security.
  • Productive assets.
  • Credit.
  • Public services.

37. Equality of Opportunity

Two people may possess identical legal rights but very different access to:

  • Quality education.
  • Assets.
  • Networks.
  • Finance.
📌 Must-Memorise

Equal Legal Rights ≠ Equal Economic Capacity

38. Growth and Social Justice

  • Economic growth contributes to social justice only when people can participate in and benefit from it.
📌 Must-Memorise

Growth Without Access → Can Preserve Inequality

Growth + Opportunity + Protection → Inclusive Development

39. Gender Justice

Gender justice seeks equal:

  • Dignity.
  • Education.
  • Employment.
  • Wages.
  • Property rights.
  • Political participation.
  • Health.
  • Safety.

40. Constitutional Basis of Gender Justice

Important provisions include:

  • Article 15 → Prohibition of sex discrimination.
  • Article 15(3) → Special provisions for women and children.
  • Article 39 → Equal-pay and worker-protection principles.

41. Education vs Gender Justice

  • Women's educational progress does not automatically ensure equal employment or economic power.
  • Barriers can include unpaid care, safety concerns, mobility restrictions and workplace discrimination.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Educational Equality ≠ Complete Gender Justice

42. Women's Agency

The long-term objective should move from:

Women's Welfare

→ Women's Agency

→ Economic Independence

→ Social Equality

43. Social Justice for Scheduled Castes

SC-focused social justice combines:

  • Reservation.
  • Educational support.
  • Economic advancement.
  • Political representation.
  • Protection against discrimination and atrocities.

44. Representation vs Dignity

  • Higher SC representation in education or public employment does not by itself eliminate caste discrimination.
  • Social dignity and freedom from everyday discrimination remain essential.
📌 Must-Memorise

SC Social Justice → Representation + Advancement + Dignity

45. Social Justice for Scheduled Tribes

Tribal communities may face specific challenges involving:

  • Geographic isolation.
  • Infrastructure gaps.
  • Displacement.
  • Traditional livelihoods.
  • Health and education access.

46. Tribal Justice

Tribal social justice requires:

  • Education.
  • Health.
  • Livelihood.
  • Habitat.
  • Community rights.
  • Cultural sensitivity.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Tribal Development ≠ Simple Assimilation

47. Backward Classes and Social Advancement

Tamil Nadu's BC/MBC/DNC framework combines:

  • Reservation.
  • Educational support.
  • Welfare measures.
  • Social advancement policies.

48. Reservation and Wider Advancement

  • Reservation improves access to specified opportunities.
  • Broader social advancement also requires:
  • Quality schooling.
  • Higher education.
  • Skills.
  • Credit.
  • Entrepreneurship.
📌 Must-Memorise

Reservation → Access

But Mobility Also Requires Capability

49. Disability Justice

  • Disability justice requires removal of physical, institutional and communication barriers.
  • Equal treatment without accessibility can still produce exclusion.

50. Reasonable Accommodation

A person with disability may require modifications to obtain meaningful equality.

Example:

  • Same staircase for everyone → Formal equality.
  • Ramp/lift where needed → Substantive equality.
📌 Must-Memorise

Accessibility → Social Justice, Not Merely Infrastructure

51. Disability-Inclusive Development

Inclusive development requires:

  • Accessible buildings.
  • Accessible transport.
  • Assistive technology.
  • Inclusive education.
  • Employment opportunity.
  • Social protection.

52. Minority Rights

  • Social justice also protects cultural and religious diversity within equal citizenship.
  • Article 29 protects specified cultural and educational interests.
  • Article 30 protects minority rights to establish and administer educational institutions.
📌 Must-Memorise

Minority Rights → Equal Citizenship + Protection of Diversity

53. Labour Justice

Social justice in labour includes:

  • Fair wages.
  • Safe working conditions.
  • Social security.
  • Maternity protection.
  • Freedom from exploitation.

54. Informal Workers

Informal workers may lack:

  • Stable contracts.
  • Social insurance.
  • Paid leave.
  • Job security.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Having Employment ≠ Having Social Security

55. Labour Justice Objective

The goal should be:

Employment

  • Fair Conditions
  • Worker Protection
  • Social Security

rather than treating any work as sufficient development.

56. Local Government and Political Inclusion

Local governments influence:

  • Drinking water.
  • Sanitation.
  • Roads.
  • Welfare.
  • Local development.

Political inclusion therefore matters at the grassroots level.

57. Articles 243D and 243T

  • Article 243D → Reservation in Panchayats.
  • Article 243T → Reservation in Municipalities.
  • These provisions support participation of SCs, STs and women under the constitutional framework.
📌 Must-Memorise

Local Representation → Voice + Influence over Resource Allocation

58. Tamil Nadu's Social-Justice Model

Tamil Nadu's model has historical roots in:

  • Non-Brahmin mobilisation.
  • Justice Party.
  • Self-Respect Movement.
  • Dravidian social reform.

Its institutional expression includes:

  • Reservation.
  • Educational assistance.
  • Nutrition.
  • Welfare.
  • Women's development.
  • Targeted support for disadvantaged communities.

59. Continuing Challenges and Future Direction

Social justice remains incomplete because challenges persist in:

  • Caste discrimination.
  • Educational quality.
  • Economic inequality.
  • Women's employment.
  • Disability accessibility.
  • Digital exclusion.
  • Regional inequality.

Intersectionality is also important because one person may face several disadvantages simultaneously.

The future direction should move from:

Access

→ Quality

→ Capability

→ Outcomes

Examples:

  • Seat provided → Education completed.
  • Benefit sanctioned → Household condition improved.
  • Reservation → Career advancement.
  • Legal right → Actual dignity.
📌 Must-Memorise

Social Justice Must Be Measured by Outcomes, Not Formal Access Alone

TNPSC Traps

  • Social Justice ≠ Poverty Relief Alone
  • Corrective Measures Do Not Necessarily Contradict Equality
  • Legal Equality ≠ Automatic Social Equality
  • Reservation Alone ≠ Complete Social Justice
  • School Admission Alone ≠ Educational Justice
  • Educational Equality ≠ Complete Gender Justice
  • Tribal Development ≠ Simple Assimilation
  • Having Employment ≠ Having Social Security

60. Rapid Revision — TNPSC Most Expected

  • Social justice means? → Fair access to rights, opportunities, resources, institutions and dignity.
  • Social justice broader than poverty relief? → Yes.
  • Four key components? → Rights + Representation + Redistribution + Recognition.
  • Formal equality? → Same rule for everyone.
  • Substantive equality? → Fair opportunity despite unequal starting conditions.
  • Preamble promises which justice? → Social, economic and political.
  • Article 14? → Equality before law and equal protection.
  • Article 15? → Prohibition of discrimination and affirmative-action framework.
  • Article 16? → Equality of opportunity in public employment.
  • Article 17? → Abolition of untouchability.
  • Article 21A? → Free and compulsory education for ages 6–14.
  • Article 23? → Prohibits trafficking, begar and forced labour.
  • Article 24? → Child-labour protection in specified hazardous employment.
  • Article 38? → Promote social order and minimise inequalities.
  • Article 39? → Livelihood, resource distribution, equal pay and worker protection.
  • Article 41? → Work, education and public assistance within State capacity.
  • Article 42? → Humane working conditions and maternity relief.
  • Article 46? → Educational and economic interests of weaker sections, especially SC/ST.
  • Article 47? → Nutrition, standard of living and public health.
  • Why does legal equality alone not guarantee social justice? → Structural discrimination can continue.
  • Affirmative action means? → Corrective measures for disadvantaged or underrepresented groups.
  • Reservation the only social-justice instrument? → No.
  • Why is representation important? → It improves inclusion and institutional participation.
  • Education's social-justice role? → Breaks inherited disadvantage.
  • Educational justice needs? → Access + Affordability + Retention + Quality.
  • Economic justice means identical incomes? → No.
  • Growth alone guarantees justice? → No.
  • Gender justice includes? → Education, employment, wages, property, safety and political participation.
  • Women's education automatically equals gender justice? → No.
  • SC social justice requires? → Representation + advancement + dignity + freedom from discrimination.
  • Tribal justice requires? → Education + health + livelihood + habitat + rights.
  • Reservation alone ensures backward-class advancement? → No.
  • Disability justice mainly requires? → Accessibility and reasonable accommodation.
  • Accessibility is only an engineering issue? → No, it is a social-justice issue.
  • Article 29? → Cultural and educational interests.
  • Article 30? → Minority educational institutions.
  • Labour justice requires? → Employment + fair conditions + worker protection.
  • Informal worker automatically socially secure? → No.
  • Article 243D? → Reservation in Panchayats.
  • Article 243T? → Reservation in Municipalities.
  • Tamil Nadu social-justice roots? → Non-Brahmin Movement + Justice Party + Self-Respect + Dravidian reform.
  • Tamil Nadu model broadly combines? → Representation + Welfare + Human Development.
  • Tamil Nadu MPI cited for 2019–21? → 2.20%.
  • Can that outcome be attributed only to reservation? → No.
  • It reflects what combination? → Growth + Education + Health + Welfare + Urbanisation + Public Services.
  • What is intersectionality? → Overlapping disadvantages affecting the same person.
  • Future social-justice goal? → Access + Quality + Capability + Outcomes.
  • Core social-justice chain? → Remove Discrimination → Expand Opportunity → Improve Representation → Build Capability → Ensure Dignity.
